title: Keep your agent. Add the review team.
description: See what MOMM means, why to use multi-model review, and how to install it, connect reviewers and inspect the private ledger.

chapters.title: Your AI. With a review team.
chapters.text: Already using Codex, Claude, or another coding agent? Mom gives it a review team. Instead of copying work between separate chats, make one request. Your selected AI tools challenge the work, and your agent brings the result back together. Keep your agent. Add the review team.

chapters.title: What MOMM means
chapters.text: Mom stands for Mixture of Model Modality. Think different AI reviewers, working with different kinds of input: code, written plans, and, where a reviewer supports it, images or documents. It's not a new model. It's a way to make your existing tools work together.
chapters.display_text: MOMM stands for Mixture of Model Modality. Think different AI reviewers, working with different kinds of input: code, written plans, and, where a reviewer supports it, images or documents. It's not a new model. It's a way to make your existing tools work together.

chapters.title: Challenge the blind spots
chapters.text: The benefit is broader scrutiny. Ask other tools to challenge an assumption, spot an overlooked risk, or suggest a simpler approach before you commit to it. Your current agent remains responsible for investigating and testing the advice. You get more challenge, without handing your project to competing editors.
chapters.display_text: The benefit is broader scrutiny. Ask other tools to challenge an assumption, spot an overlooked risk, or suggest a simpler approach before you commit to it. chapters.title: Less coordination. Parallel review.
chapters.text: If you're manually copying work between chats, you wait for answers, compare the replies, then explain the changes back to your agent. Mom runs selected reviews in parallel and collects them into one report. That's less manual coordination. It can reduce review waiting, although more reviewers still consume more quota.

chapters.title: What the evidence actually says
chapters.text: On September fourth, the public development record held three hundred and two apply decisions, and two hundred and fifty one rejections. Advice was weighed, not just accepted. These are the maintainer's records, not a customer benchmark. No universal productivity or accuracy percentage has been established.

chapters.title: Why choose this workflow?
chapters.text: Why Mom? You choose the provider tools. Keep the agent you already work in. Inspect the open source protocol and your local decision history. Code Rabbit and Qodo also offer AI review workflows. Mom is a fit when you want to coordinate your selected account based tools, with one responsible agent and explicit verification.

chapters.title: 01 / Install once
chapters.text: Here's how to start. You need Git, Node eighteen or newer, and a compatible agent. Keep the clone in a permanent folder. Open the Mom guide, copy the installation and upgrade prompt, and paste it into your agent. It finds the stable release and previews installation for your harness. Approve the plan.

chapters.title: 02 / Connect your tools
chapters.text: Open the local Setup Center. Choose your current agent, connect a reviewer with its account login, and verify the connection. Start with one; add another when its perspective earns the extra quota. The dashboard shows command line versions and guides explicit updates. Provider subscriptions and usage limits still apply.

chapters.title: 03 / Say what you want checked
chapters.text: Return to your project. Choose which providers may receive the work. Then ask: use Mom to review my changes. Investigate findings, verify any fixes, record every decision, and show me the ledger. Your agent handles the review loop. You don't have to relay each conversation yourself.

chapters.title: From opinions to decisions
chapters.text: You're seeing Mom review this film's own script. The result isn't just a score. See each reviewer's findings and suggestions together. Your agent tests material claims, applies changes the evidence supports, or rejects advice with a reason. Unfinished decisions stay visible. Agreement doesn't replace evidence.

chapters.title: Know what changed. And why.
chapters.text: Then open your private ledger. Who raised the issue? What did your agent decide? What evidence supports the change? The report, decisions, and completion record are there to inspect. That makes review easier to revisit, explain, and hand over.
